note: One-hop requirement->SCF mapping, replacing the two-hop ISO pivot (blinded 3-rater trial: 88% vs 41% defensible).

mappings.rationale: Establishing, maintaining and disseminating an approved security policy is discharged by the documentation-publication mechanism (GOV-02), its planned-interval review (GOV-03), and the programme-level governance control that defines the organisation's overall approach (GOV-01, legitimate here because the requirement is itself programme-level).
mappings.uncovered_clause: explicit senior-management approval of the policy document is only implied, not a discrete SCF mechanism

mappings.rationale: Assigning a designated individual with the mission and resources to run the security programme is GOV-04, the enforced accountability structure for teams and individuals is GOV-04.1, and the clear authority to implement controls is the authoritative chain of command in GOV-04.2.

General awareness training for all personnel is SAT-02, the 'topics relevant to the individual's role' clause is role-based training (SAT-03), and evidencing delivery on hire and at annual refresh needs the training-records mechanism (SAT-04).

Maintaining an accurate inventory of hardware, software and data assets is the asset-inventory mechanism (AST-02), and the 'with assigned owners' clause is the asset-ownership-assignment mechanism (AST-03).

Classifying information against a defined scheme is DCH-02, labelling it so handling caveats are visible is media marking (DCH-04), and defining and implementing handling procedures per classification level is the data-protection mechanism (DCH-01).

Composite: removable-media handling restrictions are DCH-12, the encryption clause is cryptographic protection of data on storage media (CRY-05.1), the tracking/custody clause is physically controlled media storage (DCH-06), and secure disposal when no longer needed is DCH-08.

Least privilege is IAC-21, enforcing access decisions on business need is access enforcement (IAC-20), and the 'reviewed regularly' clause is the periodic review of account privileges (IAC-17); the IAM umbrella was deliberately avoided.

Authenticating organisational users on systems holding the data is IAC-02, the multi-factor requirement is IAC-06, and the specific MFA-for-privileged-network-access clause is IAC-06.1; remote-access MFA is carried by requirement 7.3.

Composite: privileged access management itself is IAC-16, the 'inventoried and authorised' clause is IAC-16.1, the logging clause is auditing the execution of privileged functions (IAC-21.4), and the monitoring clause is enhanced activity monitoring of privileged users (MON-01.15).

Prompt de-provisioning on termination is IAC-07.2, the role-change clause is IAC-07.1, and the actual withdrawal of standing authorisations within the stated window is revocation of access authorisations (IAC-20.6).

Data at rest is encrypted under CRY-05, data in transit under transmission confidentiality (CRY-03), and the requirement that algorithms meet current approved standards is the use-of-cryptographic-controls mechanism (CRY-01), which is appropriate here because the requirement is itself a standards-selection obligation.

Key generation, storage and destruction across the lifecycle is CRY-09, the distribution clause is the control and distribution of keys (CRY-09.4), and the rotation clause is handled by key loss or change (CRY-09.3).

Restricting facility entry is physical access control (PES-03), the 'authorized personnel' clause is physical access authorisations (PES-02), and the entry/exit logging clause is the physical access logs mechanism (PES-03.3).

Composite: siting equipment to minimise physical/environmental damage and unauthorised access (theft) is PES-12, power disruption is the supporting-utilities mechanism (PES-07), fire is PES-08, and flood is water damage protection (PES-07.5); temperature/humidity controls were not asserted by the text.

Secure disposal or destruction of equipment so data cannot be recovered is AST-09, the wipe-or-destroy media clause is system media sanitisation (DCH-09), and the certificates-of-destruction clause is the sanitisation documentation mechanism (DCH-09.1).

Approving changes before implementation is configuration change control (CHG-02), the documented-and-tested clause is CHG-02.2 (test in non-production and document before production), and the overall process obligation is the change management programme (CHG-01).

Anti-malware deployment on systems is END-04, the 'kept current' clause is automatic signature updates (END-04.1), and 'configured for real-time protection' is the always-on protection mechanism (END-04.7).

Performing regular backups is BCD-11, the tested-for-recoverability clause is testing for reliability and integrity (BCD-11.1), and 'stored securely' is cryptographic protection of backup information (BCD-11.4).

Identification through regular scanning is VPM-06, remediation tracking to closure is VPM-02, and the ongoing-within-defined-timeframes clause is continuous vulnerability remediation activities (VPM-04).

Composite: logging and ongoing review of security events is MON-01.8, the 'logs shall be protected' clause is protection of event logs (MON-08), the retention-period clause is MON-10, and 'reviewed regularly for anomalies' is event log analysis and triage (MON-17); the MON-01 umbrella was avoided.

Isolating in-scope systems from untrusted networks is network segmentation (NET-06), the firewall/boundary clause is boundary protection (NET-03), and 'access controls at segment boundaries' is ACL-based data flow enforcement (NET-04).

Encrypting transfers over untrusted networks using strong protocols such as SFTP/HTTPS is safeguarding data over open networks (NET-12), reinforced by the transmission confidentiality mechanism (CRY-03).

Controlled remote access to in-scope systems is NET-14, the VPN/encrypted-channel clause is protection of confidentiality and integrity using encryption (NET-14.2), and the mandatory multi-factor clause is IAC-06.

Composite: spam filtering and phishing protection are the anti-phishing/anti-spam technology mechanism (END-08), encryption of sensitive information sent by email is NET-20.6, and the user-training clause is awareness training on recognising and reporting social engineering (SAT-02.2).

Establishing a documented incident response plan with defined procedures and communication protocols is IRO-04, and the defined-roles clause is the integrated incident response team mechanism (IRO-07).

Timely reporting of incidents to affected clients and third parties within a mandated window is IRO-10 (the obligation binds the supplier here, not the customer), and the 'impact assessment' element of the notification is incident classification and prioritisation (IRO-02.4).
mappings.uncovered_clause: the specific 24-hour clock and the containment-actions content of the notice are configuration of IRO-10, not separate SCF controls

mappings.rationale: Retaining incident records with details and remediation actions is the incident tracking repository (IRO-09.3), documenting incident status through resolution (the timeline clause) is IRO-09, and the lessons-learned clause is root cause analysis and lessons learned (IRO-13).

Documented recovery procedures covering the services provided are the formal BC/DR plans mechanism (BCD-01.7) within the continuity management system (BCD-01), and the 'tested' clause is contingency plan testing and exercises (BCD-04).

Composite: defined recovery time and point objectives are BCD-01.4, scoping to critical systems is identify critical assets (BCD-02), the recovery capability itself is secure recovery and reconstitution after disruption (BCD-12), and 'tested' is contingency plan testing (BCD-04).

Regularly assessing conformity of in-scope assets against the customer's requirements is control conformity monitoring (CPL-03), the remediation-plan clause is corrective action for non-conformity (CPL-02.3), and the ongoing oversight of that assessment is the controls oversight function (CPL-02).

Complying with applicable statutory and regulatory security and data protection obligations is CPL-01, and the 'identified and monitored' clause is the compliance-scope mechanism that enumerates which obligations apply (CPL-01.2).

The only clause an SCF control discharges is providing assessors the minimum necessary logical access to artifacts and physical access to facilities (CPL-03.3); the rest of the requirement is submission to the customer's own audit, which binds the auditing party rather than the assessed organisation and is deliberately not mapped to any third-party-audit control.
mappings.uncovered_clause: 'shall support SABIC security audits when requested' — the obligation to undergo an externally-initiated audit has no assessed-organisation control mechanism

mappings.rationale: Flowing the same requirements down to subcontractors by contract is TPM-05.2 within third-party contract requirements (TPM-05), and the 'verified' clause is monitoring and reviewing external service providers for compliance with those contractual requirements (TPM-08).

Committing resources to a formal continual-improvement process is GOV-01.3, the improvement-from-audits-and-assessments input is corrective action on identified non-conformity (CPL-02.3), and the improvement-from-incident-analysis input is root cause analysis and lessons learned (IRO-13).
